prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary

The SNP stands for Scotland, for Independence, and for all who live here. At Westminster, every SNP vote is a vote to complete the powers of the Scottish Parliament, to put Scotland first, and to secure a democratic referendum on Independence—triggered by a majority of SNP MPs. Until then, SNP MPs will demand more powers for Holyrood and oppose anti-Scottish measures.

Independence is a modern, 21st‑century project: a written constitution; inclusive citizenship; PR at all levels; and the Crown retained by popular consent. With Scotland’s wealth—now sent in excess to London—we will invest in people and services. We will create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations using surplus oil revenues and a Scottish Trust for Public Investment (STPI) to replace costly PFI/PPP, cutting capital costs and accelerating infrastructure renewal.

Public life will be democratized: quangos cut and scrutinized; civil service careers secured. Education will be de‑pressurized and refocused on excellence: a moratorium on churn; an Education Convention; P1–P3 classes reduced to 18 (starting in deprived areas); league tables ended; schools refurbished via STPI; statutory Gaelic‑medium provision where there is demand; free higher education with tuition fees abolished and grants rebuilt.

Our jobs strategy backs Scottish strengths: infrastructure, broadband to every community, reskilling, lighter‑touch and focused development agencies, and a reoriented tourism strategy with better access. We will devolve and redesign the New Deal, raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages, and enshrine trade union rights.

We will lead on sustainability: a State of the Nation Environmental Audit and a National Environment Plan; 12% of energy (and 25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear power and safe decommissioning; embed “precaution” and “polluter pays.” Water will remain public, with charges curbed and governance made democratic.

Health will be driven by need, not postcode. A National Health Care Commission will set strategy; HTBS decisions will be binding; free fruit in schools and healthier school meals; free dental check‑ups; prescription charges frozen and reviewed; 1,500 more nurses; hospitals modernized; waiting times halved; and free personal care for the elderly delivered.

Scotland in Europe: full EU membership as a voice among nations, not a super‑state; keep vetoes on resources, tax and constitution; euro membership only by consent. Defence: remove Trident, oppose US missile defence, build a professional Scottish Defence Force, and move to a non‑nuclear cooperative posture.

A fairer society: a national anti‑poverty strategy; dignity for asylum seekers; housing investment without wholesale stock transfer; core funding for the voluntary sector; 1,000 extra police; stronger measures against serious offenders; equality enshrined in law; stronger disability rights.

Honest taxation: no overall tax rise without mandate; a comprehensive tax review for fairness and simplicity. Immediately, cut fuel duty by 10p per gallon, funded by a 5p income tax supplement on earnings over £100,000—redistributive and revenue‑neutral.

Transport for national cohesion: invest via STPI; empower Regional Transport Authorities; reopen key rail links (including Borders and airport links), expand electrification, create national concessions, repair roads, reduce ferry fares, and abolish Skye Bridge tolls.

Rural Scotland, agriculture, and fisheries will get a level playing field in Europe, targeted support, sustainable management, and community control over land. Pensions will be linked back to earnings and winter support improved. Social security will be simplified and focused on dignity and take‑up.

We stand to use Scotland’s wealth for Scotland’s people, completing our Parliament’s powers and building a just, caring, and enterprising independent nation.
